files.lesson.md: --- order: 26 unit: trig9 node: AC9M9M03 n3 uses: [AC9M9SP01 n2] assumes: [AC9M9SP01 n2, AC9M8SP01 n1] connection: shadow-height title: Similar triangles and scale summary: "Similar triangles have the same angles. Multiply every side by the same scale factor to go from one to the other, and the area grows by that factor squared." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A flagpole is too tall to measure, but its shadow isn't. How do you use a stick to find its height?" --- A person and a flagpole stand in the sun. Each makes a right-angled triangle with its shadow, and the sun's angle is the same for both. So the two triangles are similar: one is a scaled copy of the other. Have a guess how to find the flagpole's height from them, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: scale it up ```step stage: predict insight: "Scaling the shortest side to 9 shows whether students multiply every side by the same factor or add the same amount." check: type: predict q: "A right-angled triangle has sides 3, 4 and 5. A similar triangle has a shortest side of 9. How long is its longest side?" options: - "15" - "11" - "12" - "14" actual: "15. The shortest side went from 3 to 9, a scale factor of 3, so every side is multiplied by 3: 3, 4, 5 becomes 9, 12, 15. Adding 6 to each side (9, 10, 11) would not keep the shape." ``` ## Run: the scale factor ```step stage: run insight: "The scale factor is new side ÷ old side, and it is the same for every pair of matching sides." check: { type: number, q: "A triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 is enlarged so the shortest side is 9. What is the scale factor?", answer: 3, explain: "9 ÷ 3 = 3. Every side is multiplied by 3." } ``` The 3, 4, 5 triangle and the 9, 12, 15 triangle have the same angles. Matching sides go in the same ratio. ## Investigate: matching sides ```step stage: investigate insight: "Find the scale factor from one pair of matching sides, then use it on any other side. Area scales by the factor squared." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Triangle A has sides 3, 4, 5. Triangle B is similar with its longest side 20. What is the scale factor from A to B?" answer: 4 explain: "20 ÷ 5 = 4." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $20 \\div 5$?", answer: 4, explain: "20 ÷ 5 = 4." } - check: type: number q: "Using that scale factor, how long is the shortest side of triangle B?" answer: 12 explain: "3 × 4 = 12." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jo" text: "Jo enlarges the 3, 4, 5 triangle so its longest side is 20. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: similar-by-adding explain: "Line 3: she added 15 to every side. A similar triangle needs every side multiplied by the same factor (4), not the same amount added." ``` ### Scale factor ```worked 3, 4, 5 \to ?, ?, 20 :: The longest side goes from 5 to 20. 20 \div 5 = 4 :: The scale factor. 3 \times 4 = 12, \quad 4 \times 4 = 16 :: Multiply every side by 4. \text{area} \times 4^2 = \times 16 :: Area is multiplied by the factor squared. ``` ### The factor ### Find the mistake Read Jo's working. Which line adds instead of multiplying? ## Modify: use the factor ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the factor, or going from big to small, tests that matching sides and the factor are used together." tasks: - hint: ["Find the factor from the matching pair.", "The factor is small this time: a copy that shrinks."] check: { type: number, q: "Triangle C has sides 6, 8, 10. Triangle D is similar with its shortest side 3. What is its longest side?", answer: 5, explain: "The factor is 3 ÷ 6 = 0.5, so 10 × 0.5 = 5." } - hint: ["Area scales by the factor squared.", "Factor 3 gives 3 × 3."] check: { type: number, q: "A triangle has area 6. A similar copy has all sides tripled. What is the area of the copy?", answer: 54, explain: "The area is multiplied by 3² = 9: 6 × 9 = 54." } - hint: ["Compare each angle with the matching one.", "Equal angles but a different shape is impossible."] check: { type: question, q: "Two triangles have sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 11. Are they similar?", options: ["No: the factor is 2 for two sides but 2.2 for the third", "Yes: the sides are all bigger", "Yes: 6 and 8 are doubles", "Can't tell"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Bigger isn't enough: the factor has to match.", "Two sides doubling isn't enough.", "You can test: 3, 4, 5 doubles to 6, 8, 10."], explain: "Similar triangles need the same factor for every pair. 11 ÷ 5 = 2.2 is not 2." } ``` ### A smaller copy ### Area ### Are they similar? ## Practise: scale factors ```step stage: practise insight: "Finding the factor from a matching pair and applying it." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Triangle P has sides 2, 3, 4. Triangle Q is similar with its shortest side 10. What is the scale factor?" answer: 5 explain: "10 ÷ 2 = 5." - check: type: number q: "How long is the longest side of triangle Q?" answer: 20 explain: "4 × 5 = 20." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $4 \\times 5$?", answer: 20, explain: "4 × 5 = 20." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 and one side 5. How long is the other side?" answer: 12 explain: "13² − 5² = 144, so the side is 12." ``` ### The factor ### The longest side ### Review ## Make: the flagpole ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the flagpole: the person and the flagpole make similar triangles, so one scale factor connects every pair of sides." tasks: - hint: ["Scale factor from the shadows: 8 ÷ 1.2.", "Multiply the person's height by it."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A person 1.8 m tall casts a 1.2 m shadow. At the same moment the flagpole's shadow is 8 m. How tall is the flagpole? (The lengths are made up for the task.)" steps: - ["$8 \\div 1.2 = 6.67$", "the scale factor between the shadows"] - ["$1.8 \\times 6.67 = 12$", "scale the person's height"] - ["12 m", "the flagpole's height"] answer: "12" answerLabel: "Flagpole height (m)" tolerance: 0.05 feedback: - ["8", "That is the flagpole's shadow, not its height."] - ["6.67", "That's the scale factor. Multiply the person's height by it."] criteria: - "I found the factor from matching sides (the two shadows)." - "I applied it to the person's height." - "I gave the answer in metres." explain: "The factor is 8 ÷ 1.2 = 6.67 (exactly 20 ÷ 3). 1.8 × 20 ÷ 3 = 12 m." - check: type: question q: "What would make this method wrong?" options: ["Sloping ground, or measuring at different times", "A very tall flagpole", "A short person", "A cloudy day"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Tall flagpoles are fine.", "Short people are fine.", "You need the shadows, so cloud is a problem for measuring, but not for the idea."] explain: "The two shadows must be made by the sun at the same angle, on level ground." ``` ### The height ### When it fails **Also used in** - **Maps and plans.** A scale drawing is similar to the real thing. - **Cameras and photos.** Enlarging keeps angles and changes sizes. - **Next lesson.** Using Pythagoras, trigonometry and scale together. ```teacher summary: Students use the scale factor between similar triangles to find a side, and see area scale by the factor squared (AC9M9M03, node 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can find the scale factor from matching sides. - I can use it to find another side. - I can say what happens to the area. struggle: "Adding instead of multiplying. Ask: does the 3, 4, 5 triangle keep its shape if every side gets 15 more?" before: > Students need Same angle, same ratio. The one idea: matching sides are in the same ratio; find the factor from the pair you know, then use it. Check matching sides by their angle. The flagpole and shadow lengths are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the flagpole in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student adds the same amount to each side. ask: If every side grew by 15, would the triangle keep its shape? fix: "Draw it: a thin sliver. Multiply to keep the shape." stretch: Show the areas of the 3, 4, 5 and 9, 12, 15 triangles are 6 and 54. support: A printed pair of triangles with matching sides in the same colour. leads: | Continues AC9M9M03 node 3. Where it leads: Multi-step spatial problems. exit: q: Triangle sides are multiplied by 5. By how much is the area multiplied? a: "25." explain: > Similar triangles have the same angles. Multiply every side by the same scale factor. The area is multiplied by the factor squared. ```
